transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-15 16:17 PST | Duration 48m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Optimize PM), Daniel (Silver Lake CTO), Marta (ML Eng), Ethan (Infra)
---
00:00 Maya: alright everyone, good afternoon, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, i have Liam and Priya with me, we'll do a quick intro then jump into the Optimize walkthrough focusing on batching and prefix/KV cache cost models.
00:12 Daniel: hey thanks, appreciate it. we're really keen to see what kind of cost delta we can get — our infra budget's tightening so any savings without hurting latencies would be huge.
00:20 Maya: totally understandable. quick agenda: 1) background on your traffic + constraints, 2) demo Optimize console cost model, 3) walk through batching & prefix prefetch scenarios with numbers, 4) Q&A and next steps. sound good?
00:31 Ethan: yep sounds good. for context, we run a mix of short user chat queries and longer generation tasks. peak is about 60 rps but we generally budget for 30 sustained, 50-60 bursts. latency SLO is 300ms p95 for chat.
00:45 Priya: ok that helps a lot. Marta, can you confirm average token lengths for chat vs generation?
00:50 Marta: chat is usually 20-40 tokens per request, generation tasks are 300-800 tokens. the big problem is the session-style interactions; large KV cache sizes mean token reuse could be high but we don't have a consistent prefixing strategy yet.
01:02 Liam: that's exactly where Optimize can help. we'll show a few configurations: low-batch low-latency, medium-batch balanced, and high-batch cost-first. then overlay prefix/KV cache prefetch assumptions — hit rates like 20%, 50%, 80% — and show per-token and per-session cost impacts.
01:18 Maya: quick note: we also include fallbacks — if Dedicated capacity is saturated we can route to hosted cheaper variants, but today we'll model Dedicated because your security needs looked...
01:27 Ethan: yep, we need VPC and KMS for keys, otherwise we can't move forward.
01:31 Maya: got it — we'll include private deployment notes in the follow-ups. Liam, demo time.
01:36 Liam: ok sharing screen. (screen-sharing noises) so here's the Optimize console. top right you can toggle workload profile; i'm loading a Silver Lake sample profile that matches Marta's numbers. you'll see baseline: avg seq len, concurrency, token rates.
01:52 Liam: first simulation — no batching, no prefetch. p95 latency sits at ~210ms on our dedicated medium instance, cost per 1k messages is about $X (note: numbers blurred here because transcript), this is baseline.
02:05 Marta: can you explain why latency is that low without batching?
02:08 Liam: yeah because we're not doing cross-request batching so the inference runtime serves smaller micro-batches which favor latency but cost is higher per token due to lost batching efficiency.
02:18 Liam: second simulation — conservative batching: 4-8 token windows, smart dynamic batching with 60ms aggregation timeout. that yields about 15-22% cost savings while p95 moves up to ~250ms.
02:34 Daniel: 250ms is close to our SLO of 300 so that's promising. what's the tradeoff for longer generations, like 800 tokens?
02:41 Priya: longer sequences actually increase batching opportunity because tokens stream longer; however, they also increase KV cache memory and kernel selection changes. in our sim we adjust model kernels and quantization profiles to maintain latency curve.
02:55 Liam: now for the KV/prefix cache piece — this is often where teams see large wins. we ran three hit-rate scenarios. if you get a 50% prefix hit rate (requests that reuse earlier KV state or prefix templates), cost per session drops almost linearly at first because the runtime avoids the full context recomputation.
03:14 Marta: how do you define a prefix in the sim? like conversation history vs templated prompts?
03:20 Liam: good question — we model both. prefix is any deterministic initial context or system prompt that can be cached. session KV captures conversation state; prefetch is loading expected KV into GPU memory so that subsequent calls avoid full attention recompute.
03:32 Ethan: I'm worried about memory pressure. if we prefetch a lot, do we evict others and cause thrashing?
03:38 Priya: yes that's the consideration. Optimize suggests prefetch window sizes tuned to your median session length and active sessions per GPU. we simulate eviction rates and include a hit/miss penalty in the cost model.
03:48 Liam: here's a slide — (audio: brief rustle) — shows cost curves: no-prefetch, prefetch-20%, prefetch-50%, prefetch-80%. note how batching multiplies with prefetch. at 50% prefetch and medium batching, cost falls ~35% vs baseline in our sample.
04:07 Daniel: ok that feels realistic. how sensitive is that to request arrival patterns? e.g., bursty traffic vs uniform.
04:13 Liam: quite sensitive. bursts increase batching gain up to a point because more concurrent requests means larger implicit batches, but if bursts exceed GPU concurrency limits you'll hit queueing and tail latency. we model both steady-state and burst percentile scenarios.
04:25 Marta: any concrete numbers about how much memory a KV entry takes? we have many small sessions but a few giant ones.
04:30 Priya: depends on sequence length and KV compression; we assume 2-6KB per active token entry after quantization in our default. we can plug your exact numbers into the workbook.
04:42 Ethan: network & VPC overhead — if KV is in a remote cache store, won't that add latency? we prefer in-GPU caching but that has hardware limits.
04:50 Liam: correct, in-GPU is fastest. remote networked KV adds maybe 5-40ms depending on topology; Optimize will include that as a plug-in parameter. for your setup, if you run Dedicated in your VPC with co-located Redis or NVMe caching, penalty is low.
05:05 Marta: what's the recommended approach to ramp: start with no-prefetch, add small prefix caching then increase?
05:10 Maya: most customers start with conservative batching and enable a small prefix cache (20-30% predicted hit) to observe latency impact, then iterate. we can help run an A/B POC: 1 lane baseline, 1 lane with caching and batching.
05:22 Daniel: what about model variants — do you recommend mixing cheaper quantized models for lower-fidelity tasks and full models for critical ones?
05:28 Priya: yes, routing policy is a big lever. we model multi-variant routing in the workbook: route low-cost queries to quantized variants, high-quality to full model. combined with prefix caching you can get big unit-cost wins while keeping critical answers on the high-quality path.
05:42 Ethan: any gotchas with SSO/KMS when using Private deployment for key management? we can't have keys leave our KMS.
05:48 Maya: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations; we can document exact key flow. we'll include a SOC2 + network design note in the follow-up packet.
05:56 Daniel: competitor question — we've seen CloudVendorX claim automatic prefetch heuristics. how is Redwood different?
06:02 Liam: some vendors do heuristic prefetching but they lack the integrated cost model and fine-grained eviction simulation we have in Optimize. ours simulates your workload distributions and hardware profile to avoid blind heuristics.
06:12 Marta: ok can you show the workbook now?
06:15 Liam: switching to the cost workbook. columns: workload config, batch timeout, avg batch size, prefetch hit rate, eviction rate, p95 latency, cost per 1k sessions, expected monthly cost. note the scenario rows where we change only hit rate to isolate effect.
06:30 Liam: here's one example row: medium-batch (agg=60ms), prefetch=50%, p95=270ms, cost per 1k sessions = $Y. versus no-prefetch cost = $Z. the percent delta is what we show in the chart.
06:44 Marta: what's included in the 'cost' line? GPU hours, memory, network?
06:48 Liam: GPU GPU compute and memory footprint are the main drivers; we also include network egress when remote KV is used, model variant price deltas from quantization, and a small orchestration overhead.
06:58 Daniel: do you support doing this simulation with our actual cluster sizes? we're not infinite, we have 8 A100s in our Dedicated pool.
07:05 Priya: yes, you can enter cluster topology. we ran a quick sim with 8xA100 and your 30 sustained rps profiles and came up with recommended batch settings and a suggested prefetch budget. we'll share that sheet populated with your numbers.
07:17 Ethan: one more operational question — what observability do we get to monitor cache hit rates and effective batch sizes in production?
07:23 Liam: Redwood Console has dashboarding for per-route token counts, observed batch sizes, KV hit/miss rates, and a tail-latency heatmap. you can set alerts for hit-rate regressions.
07:31 Daniel: do you keep any customer data for analytics? we need to know about retention and PII.
07:36 Maya: we only store telemetry and aggregated metrics — no PII unless explicitly allowed. for Private we can disable telemetry retention and stream logs to your syslog. we'll give specifics in the security pack.
07:49 Marta: small note: our prompts include customer PII sometimes during dev tests — we need guaranteed redaction options.
07:55 Priya: we have redaction pipeline examples and can enable local pre-processing or inline redaction via policy. will include in follow-up.
08:02 Liam: moving toward the wrap — quick recap: batching gives you X-Y% cost wins but increases p95; prefix/KV prefetch compounds savings if hit rates are reasonable; memory and eviction model matters; start conservative and POC at small scale.
08:17 Daniel: sounds good. any expected anomalies we should watch for during POC?
08:20 Liam: noisy neighbors in Shared mode, GC pauses in old kernels, and misestimated hit rates. we usually recommend synthetic load tests that mirror 95th percentile bursts to validate tail latency.
08:29 Ethan: ok let's talk timelines. we want to run the POC asap.
08:32 Maya: we'll send the cost workbook and SOC2/KMS/VPC docs tomorrow, Liam will run the simulator with your exported trace and return a populated scenario by Jan 20, then propose a 48h benchmark window Jan 22-23.
08:44 Daniel: that's tight but workable. thanks.
08:47 Maya: thanks all. we'll email notes and next steps.
08:50 (end recording)
